title: Flash Onramp: POC Sprint Outline & Success Criteria — Meridian Retail
body:
Goal: Run a 3-week, production-proximate POC to validate in-store conversational assistant for Meridian Retail. Focus is on latency, relevance, and integration ergonomics with Meridian’s POS and catalog APIs. Output: decision memo recommending one of: move to Dedicated reserved capacity, continue on Hosted with optimization, or pause.

Scope & non-goals:
- In-scope: chat-based product lookup, receipt summarization, and a short re-ranking pipeline for top-5 results. Model variants to test: open-llm-7b-quant and community-13b trimmed for latency.
- Out-of-scope: end-to-end checkout flows, real-time payments, customer account management.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end response <= 450ms for single-turn product lookup under baseline load (5 RPS)
- Relevance: Top-1 accuracy >= 82% on merchant-provided 200-item eval set; NDCG@5 >= 0.68
- Availability: 99.5% uptime during business hours (M-F 8am-8pm PST) for test windows
- Cost: Token cost per session not to exceed $0.045 for the conversational happy path
- Integration: Working webhook and POS-sync within 7 business days (able to fetch SKU metadata and aliases)
- Rollout readiness: Canary test executed and rollback path validated in Redwood Console

Team & roles:
- Customer PM: Hannah Ruiz (Meridian) — business acceptance, eval data
- SE lead: Aisha Patel — technical ownership, deployment config
- Infra eng: Jordan Kim — Dedicated cluster sizing & autoscaling policy
- Dev contact: Luis Fernandez (Meridian eng) — API credentials, test harness
- QA / Eval: Mei Chen — prompt set, eval metrics, regression checks
- CS sponsor: Samir Rao — success plan and acceptance sign-off

Assumptions & constraints:
- Meridian will provide a representative catalog dump (CSV/JSON) and 250 sample queries by Day 2.
- Customer allows test traffic to be routed through Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2.
- No PI/PHI in test dataset; PII must be redacted before ingestion.

POC timeline (compact sprint):
- Week 0 (Kickoff, Day 0–2): credential exchange, data handoff, baseline infra spin-up, smoke test
- Week 1 (Day 3–9): model variant integration, prompt engineering, initial eval runs, latency profiling
- Week 2 (Day 10–16): load test (5–20 RPS), caching experiments (prefix caching enabled), routing fallback checks
- Week 3 (Day 17–21): acceptance window (4 business days), canary replay, sign-off meeting, decision memo

Technical checklist (must-pass items):
- API keys provisioned and scoped (prod/test segregation)
- Catalog ingestion job created; embeddings for search persisted and linked to SKU IDs
- Query path instrumented with tracing to Redwood Console; token-level billing visible
- Autoscaling policy configured for Dedicated pool (min 1 node, burst to 3)
- KV cache enabled for repeated prefixes; cache hit rate target > 20% during load test
- Fallback policy: on capacity pressure route to hosted smaller model with preserved output schema

Evaluation & acceptance procedure:
- Mei will run the merchant-provided eval set and an additional 500 synthetic queries.
- Produce a single-sheet scoreboard with metrics: p95 latency, top-1 accuracy, NDCG@5, per-session cost, error rate.
- Acceptance requires meeting 4 of 5 measurable success criteria AND product manager sign-off. If cost or latency misses, document optimizations and a path to re-run.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Catalog aliases cause mismatches —> Mitigation: implement fuzzy alias map and increase top-K retrieval to 10; evaluate NDCG uplift.
- Risk: Unexpected token cost spike —> Mitigation: use token caps, enable response truncation and sampling temperature controls.
- Risk: Network egress limits on customer side —> Mitigation: run Local proxy during tests and capture metrics.

Workshop notes (Kickoff meeting 2024-10-22):
- Customer emphasized offline evaluation is most important; demo is secondary.
- Meridian’s devs requested a simple webhook alt for SKU enrichment rather than full API integration initially.
- Action item: Meridian to provide full catalog and 250 queries by 10/24 (Hannah).
- Action item: Jordan to provision Dedicated pool and share access details by 10/25.
- Unresolved: Which model variant is default for canary? SE to recommend by 10/26 after initial runs.

Deliverables and handoff:
- Week 1 deliverable: baseline scoreboard + latency profile (SE & QA)
- Week 2 deliverable: load test report + cache tuning notes (Infra & SE)
- Final deliverable: decision memo with recommended next step, runbook for production migration, and roll-back checklist (SE + CS)

Next steps (short list):
- Aisha: draft decision memo template and initial runbook (due 11/01)
- Mei: create eval harness and upload to shared artifacts (due 10/28)
- Luis: provide API sandbox credentials and sample catalog (due 10/24)
- Jordan: confirm Dedicated nodes + autoscaling policy applied (due 10/25)
- All: join recurring standup M/W/F 09:30 PT — first sync 10/23

Notes to self: keep prompts minimal for first pass; prefer deterministic sampling and strong rejection sampling for SKU hallucination checks. Document prompt failures with example inputs for model team.
